title: AIDM Campaign Pack
description: Structured adventure module import format for AIDM campaigns. Every record, startingState, directorRules, gmNotes, hiddenSceneNotes and marketplace value is bounded on import: containers may nest at most 12 levels below the record (the record itself is level 0), strings may be at most 4000 characters, objects at most 80 keys (keys at most 120 characters) and lists at most 150 items. Content beyond a bound is rejected with error_code pack_content_out_of_bounds and its JSON path; nothing is truncated.

schemaVersion.description: Campaign pack schema version. AIDM currently accepts 1, 1.0, and 1.0.0 as version 1.

checkpointId.description: Initial active checkpoint; defaults to the first checkpoint.

clock.description: When the adventure begins. Without it the party starts on day 1 in the morning.

flags.description: Copied verbatim into the session's authoritative flags.

campaignFlags.description: Accepted alias of flags; keys in flags win on conflict. Prefer flags.

partyStatus.description: GM-only starting brief, stored at campaignPack.startingBrief.partyStatus. Never shown to players.

partyNotes.description: GM-only starting brief, stored at campaignPack.startingBrief.partyNotes. Never shown to players.

secret.description: Counts among the adventure's secrets (found when discovered); the chronicle tells how many were never found.

map.description: World map settings: title, terrain and the layout seed.

routes.description: Route styles between connected locations (default road for every adjacency).

tieLines.description: Lines that bring a hero's own threads into the adventure. Each fires at most once per adventure, for a present hero who has that tie; see docs/campaign_packs.md.

talkRequirement.description: When a topic is offered (or a check DC applies): every key given must hold. flags: each flag equals its value, an unset flag counting as false; clueIds: the party knows each clue; itemIds: the hero holds each item; topicIds: this person has told each topic; encounterResolvedIds: each encounter is complete; dispositionAtLeast: the person's disposition (-2 hostile to 2 loyal) is at least this; remembers: the person remembers this key of the hero; anyOf: at least one of these requirements holds.

talkAffect.description: Another person's disposition moved by this: only when that person is known and present (and the when flag holds). line is the story beat shown; without it the engine writes one.

talkEffects.description: What a told topic, a reaction or a callback does. givesItems go to the hero; disposition moves this person; promise sets that flag and records the hero's word (kept or broken only by keepsPromise / breaksPromise naming it); remember and forget are memory keys of this hero.

promise.description: The promise this records, by its id, or with the lines the end of the story reads for it: keptText once its keeping act has happened, brokenText once broken (by its breaking act or when brokenWhen's flags hold), openText while it is still open.

clock.description: Pressure with a cause. A clock of the place the party is at (its location's, or an encounter's there that has not begun) starts once startWhen holds (at once without it) or an affordance starts it; it then moves one step for each of its causes: each listed flag the first time it is set, each listed object action the first time it succeeds, and every everyTurnsAfterStart turns taken there outside a fight. A step's text is told by the engine as written, the turn's one director note; its effects apply. It never moves without a cause.

nudge.description: A one-line pointer the director tells, as written, when four turns at the place have brought nothing but hints (once): "Tovin keeps glancing at the stable."

talkDcWhen.description: A requirement with the DC that applies while it holds, or noCheck: told without a check.

talkCheck.description: A check the engine rolls for the hero. dcWhen: requirements with their own dc (or noCheck: told without a check); the first that holds decides.

talkTopic.description: Something a person tells once. ask topics are offered as "Ask about {label}", say topics by their label as written. Offered while requires holds and it is not told; typed words holding the label or a keyword (whole words) choose it. A failed check offers it again only in a later conversation. private: offered only when no other known person stands in the hero's room.

talkReaction.description: What a person does with a speech act (promise, show, threaten, offer, claim, apologise; about narrows it to an item, a clue, or for a claim authority or identity). The first entry that matches is used; once spends it.

talkCallback.description: An earlier act brought back once: when the person remembers when.remembers of a hero and when.flags hold, at the event (arrival, at atLocationId when given; fight_end; rest; topic:<id>), with the person known and present, text opens the narration, effects apply for that hero and offers opens those topics.

sceneObject.description: A door, lock, container, object or hazard in a scene. Any other authored field (state, requirements, transitions, discoveries) is kept as written.

allowedActions.description: Limits the actions the object supports to these; without it the object's kind and flags decide.

actionLabels.description: The words the Story screen offers for an action, for example {"inspect": "Read the caravan ledger"}. An action without one reads "Examine {name}", "Search {name}", "Open {name}" and so on. The linter warns about a label for an action the object does not support.

inspires.description: Inspiration for the hero who does the action, with its reason, for example {"search": "a secret uncovered"}. The linter warns about an action the object does not support.

actionText.description: DM-side text the narrator draws on when an action resolves, for example what reading a ledger shows. Kept in session state like description and never sent to players. The linter warns about text for an action the object does not support.

proper.description: The name is a proper noun, so refusals read "Excalibur is locked." rather than "The Excalibur is locked.". A name that starts with "The" is never given another article.

contents.description: What a container holds: items, or coin as {"currency": {"gp": 15}}. A successful search (or opening) outside a fight puts them in the searching hero's pack in the same turn; an item marked "leave": true stays in the scene to be taken by choice.

leave.description: Left where it lies when found (heavy, dangerous, or the players' choice to make): it is never taken by the search that finds it.

choiceActions.description: Actions that are alternatives to one another, such as the fates of a ward. The Story screen shows each of them that can be taken as its own suggestion, together, before the others. The linter errors on an action the object does not support.

affects.description: People's dispositions moved when the named action succeeds, for example {"break": [{"npcId": "npc_osric_hale", "disposition": -1, "line": "Osric Hale will remember that."}]}; each applies only when that person is known and present.

zoneId.description: The zone of its location it stands in; without it, the location's startZoneId.

tags.description: What plans can do with the object (W9-SCENE effects): exit, barrier, light, fire, cover, heavy, fragile, rope, animal, crowd, vehicle, container, noise, high_ground.

guards.description: The way (another object's id) a heavy or vehicle object blocks when it is used to obstruct.

exposedBy.description: Hidden until an expose effect in its zone reveals it.

affordances.description: Authored plans on the object, offered like other actions (at most two as suggestions) and chosen by typed words holding their keywords.

onFail.description: Failing forward, by action: a failed check applies this instead of coming up empty; with noRetry the slow retry is not offered.

usableInCombat.description: The actions a hero can take on this object during a fight, on their own turn while their action is unspent; taking one spends the action. Every other action is refused in a fight with "Not while the fight is on.".

resolvesEncounter.description: When the named action succeeds, the encounter is completed with the outcome through the same path a combat ending uses (consequences, once-only rewards, objectives); its combat, if active, ends at once and its trigger never fires afterwards. The linter errors on an unknown encounter or an outcome the encounter does not allow.

triggerable.description: true offers the trigger action on an object that is not a hazard. Read only when it is exactly true.

repeatable.description: true lets the object be triggered again after it has been triggered; otherwise the trigger action is refused until the object is reset (hazards can be reset). Read only when it is exactly true.

questPredicate.description: Quest objective predicate evaluated by the quest engine after every applied change. Event keys (eventType|event|changeType, actorId, targetActorId, targetId, objectId, itemId, itemName, npcId, locationId, encounterId, participantId, endReason, flagKey, checkpointId, objectiveId, questId, quantityAtLeast|amountAtLeast) match the applied change exactly (strings case-insensitively). State keys (atLocationId; locationId and flagKey + flagValue|equals when no event type is given; possessesItemId|possessesItemName with optional actorId and quantityAtLeast; objectiveIds + objectivePolicy all|any) are checked against the state after the change. Event and state keys in one predicate must all hold. all|allOf and any|anyOf hold lists of predicates; entries that are not objects are ignored and a combinator with no predicate is never satisfied; other keys next to a combinator are ignored. Any other key is ignored by the engine and reported by the linter.

flagCondition.description: A flag predicate, or anyOf a list of them (holds when any one does).

encounterAdjustment.description: Applied when the encounter's combat is created, before party scaling, while its flag holds. text is a line the narration must say.

hpMultiplier.description: Multiplies that enemy's hit points, together with the party scaling multiplier.

removeEnemyIds.description: Enemy groups that stay away; they are gone before the party's most enemies is applied.

flagPredicate.description: A fail-closed predicate evaluated against the persisted authoritative state flags. It does not inspect narration or model output.

connectedLocationIds.description: The only adjacency structured travel uses. A location without it cannot be reached or left by structured travel.

npcIds.description: The people here. Arrival meets each one not yet known (they join the known people and the scene's present cast) unless their hidden or hiddenUntil keeps them away.

questIds.description: Merged into the scene's active quests on arrival.

interactables.description: Doors, locks, containers and objects restored into the scene on arrival (and at the start when this is the starting location and the starting scene lists none).

sceneState.description: Optional scene-local overrides; a collection here wins over the top-level one.

gmNotes.description: Stored in the operator catalog only; never sent to players or the DM prompt.

onEnter.description: Trusted consequences applied once, on the first arrival.

mapPosition.description: Position on the 0-100 world map grid; computed at import when missing.

ambience.description: The generated sound bed the Story view plays here; without it the bed follows the map icon and the clock.

weather.description: Shown behind the story; rain also adds the sound of rain over the place's bed.

zones.description: The rooms or areas the place divides into. Each hero stands in one; arrival puts every hero in startZoneId. A hero acts only on things and people in their own zone, steps next door first for one in an adjacent zone, and is refused for anything further off. Without zones the place is one area.

startZoneId.description: The zone every hero stands in on arrival; required when the location has zones.

description.description: One sentence told the first time a hero steps in.

adjacentTo.description: The zones one move away; adjacency goes both ways whichever zone lists it.

exit.description: true lets the party leave the place (travel) from here; when no zone is marked, every zone is an exit.

rest.description: true lets heroes rest here; when no zone is marked, every zone allows it.

moveLabel.description: The words of the offered move into this zone ("Go into the common room"); otherwise "Go to" and the zone's name.

disposition.description: How the person starts out towards the party: hostile, wary, neutral, warm or loyal (anything else starts neutral). In play it moves from -2 to 2 and players see the word.

greeting.description: Told when a conversation with the person opens for the first time.

topics.description: What the person can be talked about (stored in the operator catalog; a line reaches players only when told). Without topics a person tells their knows lines one by one.

reacts.description: Authored reactions to speech acts; without one the engine's defaults apply.

callbacks.description: Remembered acts that return to play.

caresAbout.description: Item or clue ids that move the person when shown.

epilogues.description: What became of the person, told at the end of the story when the party met them: the first entry whose when holds (flags, dispositionAtLeast, companion: they walk with the party); an entry without when is the default, one without text gives no line.

wants.description: What an offer must meet: item ids or coin:<gold pieces>. Never shown to players.

believes.description: Claims the person takes as true without a check when ifFlags hold and the hero holds ifItems. Never shown to players.

description.description: Shown to players when no playerDescription is set.

personality.description: Stored in the operator catalog only; never shown to players.

motivation.description: Stored in the operator catalog only; never shown to players.

knows.description: Stored in the operator catalog only; never shown to players.

secret.description: Stored in the operator catalog only; never shown to players. A boolean true (or a yes/true string) instead hides the whole NPC from players.

useInPlay.description: Stored in the operator catalog only; never shown to players.

ifSkipped.description: Stored in the operator catalog only; never shown to players.

gmNotes.description: Stored in the operator catalog only; never shown to players.

trueName.description: Stored in the operator catalog only; never shown to players.

hidden.description: Never met by arriving at a place that lists this person in its npcIds; only an operator or an explicit change reveals them.

hiddenUntil.description: Met by arriving at a place that lists this person (or while the party is there) only once this flag holds; equals defaults to true.

zoneId.description: The zone of their location they stand in; without it, its startZoneId.

prerequisiteObjectiveIds.description: Objectives of the same quest that must be completed first; until then this objective is blocked.

completeWhen.description: An objective with no completeWhen, failWhen or prerequisites can only be completed by an operator; narration cannot complete it.

singularName.description: One of this enemy, when name is a group ("Ashmarked Cutthroat" for "Ashmarked Cutthroats").

proper.description: The name is a proper noun ("The Hollow Marshal"), never pluralised or given an article.

challengeTier.description: "boss" makes the enemy stand its ground: it never yields or retreats above a quarter of its hit points.

pronoun.description: How the narration refers to one of this enemy; "it" when absent ("they" for a proper name).

captiveKnows.description: What one of this enemy tells, a line each time it is questioned, once the party holds it captive (bound or yielded after a fight).

barks.description: Short lines this enemy speaks or shows in a fight. A line in quotation marks is speech (printed with its speaker); a line without is a described tell (printed as written). start: in the fight's first narration; hurt: the first time one of them is at half its hit points or less; turning: when one yields, flees or is captured; taunt: in place of a turn that only fills time, at most once per enemy every two rounds.

durationRounds.description: How many of the target's turns the ability's conditionsApplied last, each ending at the end of the target's turn (default 1: until the end of its next turn). An ability with a save repeats it at the end of each of those turns; success ends the conditions.

encounterRewardSpec.description: Compact reward object or explicit typed reward records. Supported rewards include XP, currency, items, flags, and quest events.

clocks.description: Clocks live while the party is at one of the encounter's locations and the encounter has not begun.

setup.description: Read-aloud text told when the encounter's fight starts, before the first blows and before any adjustment line. It is not part of the player snapshot.

stakes.description: A note for the operator (a string, never shown to players), or what the fight is about (W9-SCENE): a list of item, person and route stakes.

enemyGoal.description: What the enemies try to do: take_and_flee makes the first enemy the runner, who takes the item stake and escapes by the route stake.

secondaryGoal.description: silence: one enemy that is not the runner goes for the person stake each turn it is not engaged.

results.description: Applied in order when the fight ends, each whose when holds: flags, a scene fact, dispositions, a lead and its text, told as written.

minEnemies.description: For a party under four: the scaled encounter never has fewer enemies (the first group regains them).

gmNotes.description: Stored in the operator catalog only; never shown to players.

reward.description: Compatibility alias for common successful-outcome encounter rewards.

rewards.description: Common rewards for victory, surrender, negotiation, or objective completion.

partyAllocation.description: Default allocation policy by reward type. Supported values are split, each, first, and actor.

outcomes.description: Outcome-specific rewards, consequences, quest events, allocation policy and affects (people's dispositions moved by that outcome, each only when the person is known and present). Prefer victory, defeat, retreat, surrender, negotiation, and objective_completion keys.

outcomeRewards.description: Compatibility map of combat outcome to reward specification.

outcomeConsequences.description: Map of combat outcome to bounded state consequences.

questEvents.description: Stable gameplay events offered to linked mechanical quests after the encounter ends.

onDefeat.description: A list of consequences of a defeat, or (W9-SCENE) what a beaten party wakes to instead of the encounter re-arming: the zone they wake in, its text, flags and stake states; the encounter is then complete.

once.description: Fire the trigger only once (default true).

when.description: The trigger fires only while this flag condition holds.

unless.description: The trigger does not fire while this flag condition holds (any one, for anyOf).

adjustments.description: What the party knows adjusts the fight: each adjustment whose flag holds when the combat is created weakens one enemy group or keeps groups away, and its text is narrated.

scaling.description: Counts and HP are authored for four player characters and scale down for a smaller party; false disables that.

allowParley.description: Its enemies may negotiate, surrender, yield or retreat from the first round; otherwise only at half HP or less, once their side has lost a member, or from round 4 once hurt.

zoneId.description: Where its fight happens: a zone of one of its locations. Heroes standing in another zone start the fight far off, having come running.

startBand.description: Where the group stands as the fight starts: melee and near are a move away from the heroes, far is out of reach until a hero advances.

minHp.description: For a party under four: no enemy of the group has less maximum HP than this after scaling.

lethalDefeat.description: true makes a defeat in this encounter's fight decisive: when every hero is down it fails a checkpoint naming the encounter in failWhen, so the story takes that checkpoint's failure route. It means nothing else: lethal or not, a beaten party wakes at the end of the fight with 1 HP one phase later, the encounter re-arms, and a failure never advances onto a terminal checkpoint. Read only when it is exactly true.

summary.description: Used as the segment description when description is absent.

locationId.description: Without a trigger, the segment triggers automatically when the party's current location is this location.

trigger.description: A plain string is a comma-separated keyword list matched against the player's message. Without a trigger the segment is manual, unless it has a locationId.

keywords.description: keyword triggers: a list (or comma-separated string) matched against the player's message.

match.description: keyword triggers: any (default) or all keywords must appear.

location_contains.description: state triggers: substring of the current location name or id.

quest_contains.description: state triggers: substring of an active quest's id, title, stage, summary or objectives.

locationId.description: location triggers: fires when the current location id equals this id.

teaser.description: One line about what lies ahead, told when the chapter this checkpoint closes ends.

chapterBreak.description: When this checkpoint completes the chapter ends: the story gains its chapter-end entry (what the players decided, what is still open, the teaser) and the next action begins the next chapter.

decisionLines.description: WHAT YOU DECIDED at the chapter's end: every line whose when holds, at most five shown. when may test flags, stakes ({"<encounterId>.<stakeId>": "<state>"}) and remembers ({"npcId", "key"} or a list of them).

endingVariants.description: On a terminal checkpoint: the first variant whose flag holds names the ending and tells it, everywhere the ending is shown; with none, the checkpoint's own title and summary do.

branchWhen.description: Makes this checkpoint eligible for automatic branch selection only when the authoritative flag predicate matches.

completeWhen.description: When present, only these conditions complete the checkpoint; any one of them suffices. Other keys (for example summary) are ignored.

locationIds.description: The party is at one of these locations.

segmentIds.description: One of these segments has triggered.

objectiveIds.description: One of these objectives is completed (scoped to questIds when given).

questIds.description: One of these quests is completed.

encounterIds.description: One of these pack encounters ended with an allowed outcome.

clueIds.description: All of these clues have been discovered.

flags.description: All of these flags match the authoritative flags, with branchWhen comparison rules.

anyOf.description: Encounter outcome labels (defeat, flee, surrender, bargain, negotiate, objective, resolve, success, ...). Prose sentences are ignored.

failWhen.description: Reads only questIds, objectiveIds and encounterIds; other keys are ignored.

gmNotes.description: Stored with the checkpoint for operators; never shown to players.

directorRules.description: Only the six listed keys (or their snake_case forms) are read; any other key is ignored and reported by the linter.

name.description: Scene name; title is accepted as an alias.

visibleDetails.description: Player-facing details of the opening scene.

hiddenSceneNotes.description: GM-only notes kept on the opening scene; never shown to players.

interactables.description: Opening-scene objects. When absent or empty, the starting location's own interactables are used.

hazards.description: Opening-scene hazards. When absent or empty, the starting location's own hazards are used.

encounterTrigger.description: Starts the encounter by itself: on first entering a location, while a checkpoint is active, when a flag is set to a value, or when an object action succeeds.

catalog.description: A price-list key; priced by the trade rules.

itemId.description: The id the purchased item keeps in the inventory.

storyFlag.description: A flag narration may set: only this key, only to one of values (default [true]).

affordance.description: An authored plan on a scene object (W9-SCENE): its effect, label, keywords, check and what it changes.

onFail.description: What a failed check does instead of coming up empty (W9-SCENE failing forward).

stake.description: What a fight is about: an item (itemId), a person (npcId, optionally only when a flag holds) or a route (objectId).

tieLine.description: A line told for a hero who has the tie. Tokens: {name} and {relation} (seeking), {burden} (burden), {hero} (any kind).

desire.description: For a desire line: the desire it fires for.

at.description: When it fires: an object action, the first arrival at a location, an encounter starting (with its setup), a long rest, or an ending variant (by the flag that chooses it; appended to that ending's text).
